The Assistant Director for Curricular Initiatives provides day-to-day operational leadership and analytical support for an array of important programs, including First-Year Pathways, Big Ideas Courses, Freshmen & Sophomore Seminars, and On The Same Page. This position leverages expert knowledge of curriculum design, program assessment, high-impact practices, mentorship, and academic policy to expand and improve student and faculty experience across this portfolio.
Programmatic Oversight and Leadership

The Assistant Director plays a consultative role in the administration and evaluation of the College of Letters & Science's Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF L&S), the Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program (URAP), and Rose Hills Summer Scholarships. This position advances strategic initiatives emerging from decanal mandates, coordinating with communications experts and policy and data analysts to undertake outreach, convene advisory committees, and collect data. The Assistant Director for Curricular Initiatives works closely with colleagues in the Office of Undergraduate Research and Scholarships to ensure the integration of scaffolding learning, pedagogical best practices, and design assessments to demonstrate impact. Additionally, this position serves as an ambassador for the ideals of a liberal arts education and an advocate for embedding experiential learning in curricular enrichment initiatives.

Provides leadership and programmatic oversight in the domain of curricular and cocurricular engagement, affecting undergraduates campus-wide. With six large-scale curricular and research programs (Freshman and Sophomore Seminars, First-Year Pathways, Big Ideas Courses, On the Same Page, Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program) and two co-curricular research programs (SURF L&S and Rose Hills Summer Scholarships) already established, a majority of this time is spent in activities necessary to administering and improving them, including but not limited to annual planning, recruiting students and faculty participants, guiding faculty in course development, developing and overseeing budgets, event planning, overseeing selection processes, and assessing and improving each program.
Exercises independent decision-making, complex problem-solving, strategic oversight, and savviness in escalating matters to higher leadership.

Collaborates with departments to build and maintain course clusters, organizing recruitment events, program assessments, providing guidance and support to staff who handle program promotion and enrollment processes.
Policy and Analytical Support

Sets policies and supports communications planning for the academic engagement programs under the position's portfolio, including selection criteria and criteria for participation, eligibility for funding, class size, and learning outcomes driving the assessment parameters.

Leads efforts to conduct highly complex analyses across these diverse programs to ensure each program fulfills its stated educational and enrichment outcomes, producing compelling reports with varied data.
Advocates solutions to organizational or research program issues, including developing and administering new systems, policies, processes, or programs as needed.
Provides operational and analytical support, researching established major requirements, pre-professional track programs, and general educational requirements.
Develops proposals and recommendations to guide and support a broader strategic direction for the program, initiative, or organizational goal.
Operational Coordination and Research
Works in coordination with Project Policy Analyst 3 to meet program goals and ensure operations (scheduling, grant funds, faculty correspondence) are running smoothly.

Supports executive decision-making and problem-solving around complex or unusual situations in these areas, ensuring that procedures fulfill departmental and divisional goals and align with campus policy.
Undertakes higher-level research about specific breadth and major requirements, curriculum and pedagogy, as well as established and emerging high-impact practices.
Researches and summarizes best practices in the field.
Oversees COCI approval processes for newly proposed courses.
Strategic Initiative Development

Translates decanal ideas for the enrichment of undergraduate education into fully operational programs, in consultation with supervisors, securing all necessary approvals, developing procedures and timelines.
Provides ad hoc support for policy-related initiatives related to undergraduate experience and expert guidance on academic policy development.

Helps the director lead monthly staff meetings and supports coordination around communications strategy across units and programs within purview, including monitoring SPA accounts and updating websites.
Fluency with the core values and history of liberal arts education.
Capacity to engage scholarly stakeholders on an array of advanced interdisciplinary initiatives.
Advanced knowledge of curriculum development and design.
Broad knowledge of advanced research and pedagogy across multiple domains.
Expert project management skills, particularly in support of undergraduate educational initiatives.
Thorough knowledge of high-impact practices and experiential learning.
Skills in designing and administering surveys and assessments.
Advanced knowledge of general education requirements, major pathways, and academic policy.
Advanced analytical skills and ability to iteratively develop administrative processes, protocols, and procedures.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with all levels of staff both verbally and in writing.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
